title: Grade 11 Physics — Units and Measurements & Motion in a Straight Line
description: Units and Measurements and Motion in a Straight Line practice questions
subject: physics

questions.question: The SI base unit of mass is:
questions.explanation: The kilogram (kg) is the SI base unit of mass. The seven SI base units are metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, and candela.

questions.question: The dimension of force is:
questions.explanation: F = ma. Dimensions: [M][LT⁻²] = [MLT⁻²]. The unit of force is the Newton = kg·m/s².

questions.question: Significant figures in 0.00420 are:
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant. 0.00420 has 3 significant figures: 4, 2, and the trailing 0 after 2 (which is significant as it follows a non-zero digit after the decimal).

questions.question: Which of the following pairs has the same dimensional formula?
questions.explanation: Pressure = Force/Area = [MLT⁻²]/[L²] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²]. Stress = Force/Area = [ML⁻¹T⁻²]. They have the same dimensions.

questions.question: The principle of homogeneity of dimensions states that:
options: All terms in a physical equation must have the same unit
All terms in a valid physical equation must have the same dimensions
Dimensions can be added or subtracted
questions.explanation: The principle of homogeneity: in any valid physical equation, every term must have the same dimensional formula. This is used to check equations and derive new ones.

questions.question: Least count of a measuring instrument determines its:
questions.explanation: The least count is the smallest value that can be measured directly. A smaller least count means higher precision (finer measurements).

questions.question: Dimensional analysis can be used to:
questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis checks if an equation is dimensionally consistent. It cannot determine dimensionless constants (like 2π in time period of a pendulum T = 2π√(L/g)).

questions.question: Average acceleration is defined as:
questions.explanation: Average acceleration = Δv/Δt = (v₂ − v₁)/(t₂ − t₁). It is a vector quantity with SI unit m/s².

questions.question: For uniform motion, the velocity-time (v-t) graph is:
questions.explanation: Uniform motion means constant velocity (acceleration = 0). On a v-t graph, this appears as a horizontal straight line (constant v).

questions.question: A body is dropped from rest. After 2 seconds (g = 10 m/s²), its velocity is:
The distance covered by a body starting from rest with uniform acceleration a in time t is:
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at². With u = 0: s = ½at². This is the second equation of motion for uniform acceleration.

questions.question: A body thrown vertically upward reaches maximum height when:
questions.explanation: At the highest point, the velocity (upward component) becomes zero momentarily before the body starts falling back. Acceleration due to gravity (g = 10 m/s² downward) is always present.

questions.question: The third equation of motion v² = u² + 2as is derived by:
options: Eliminating time t between the first two equations
questions.explanation: From v = u + at → t = (v−u)/a. Substituting into s = ut + ½at² and simplifying gives v² = u² + 2as.

questions.question: Relative velocity of object A with respect to B is:
questions.explanation: Relative velocity of A with respect to B = vₐ − v_B. If both move in the same direction, relative velocity is the difference; if opposite, it is the sum.
